purpose: Provide recruiting, screening, browser and portfolio-analysis agents with a structured, factual, neutral representation of the same person shown in Human Mode.

machine_readable_files.content: Candidate identity, positioning, capabilities, experience, projects, external evidence, roles, skills, links
Structured candidate record: identity, education, experience, projects, skills, open source, achievements, roles, limitations
Capabilities with pointers to evidence, plus an explicit non-claims list
Evidence graph: claim → capability → project → implementation → result → verification
Index of indexable pages (Human Mode and Agent Mode)
Crawler policy: legitimate crawlers allowed, nothing hidden

content_guarantees: The complete candidate story is present in the served HTML; no critical information requires JavaScript, hover, canvas, or scrolling to reveal.
Agent Mode uses semantic HTML5 (main, article, section, header, nav, h1–h4, dl, ul) with stable IDs.
Agent Mode loads with zero JavaScript dependencies.
Skills in Agent Mode are reproduced verbatim from Human Mode; no technology was added, removed, or upgraded.
Every quantitative claim is attributed to a source (portfolio, résumé PDF, GitHub API, LeetCode API) with a check date.
Unverifiable claims are labelled explicitly rather than omitted silently.

Agent Mode includes two recruiter-oriented sections rendered as plain evidence summaries: "Why Interview" (evidence areas, no verdicts) and "Where This Evidence Applies" (role → relevant capabilities → evidence, no scores or rankings).

Claims carry qualitative evidence status labels (public_repo · private_available_on_request · external_validation · documented_experience · self_reported · experimental); no numeric fit score, ranking, or percentage is computed.
mode_position: Agent Mode is a neutral structured record of the same facts shown in Human Mode: identity, capabilities, experience, projects, evidence, and verification status — without fabrication, exaggeration, invented evidence, rankings, or preference language.
not_claimed: No autonomous agent or chatbot is hosted here.
No personal-data API or outreach API exists on this site.
No scoring, ranking, or fit-percentage is computed for candidates.

No cloaking: Human Mode and Agent Mode describe the same candidate with the same factual claims; Agent Mode adds structured context, evidence relationships, verification status, and technical topic indexes.

evidence_labels.note: Qualitative labels only — no numeric evidence scores, fit percentages, or rankings are computed. `status` always holds exactly one value from `values`; `qualifiers` holds any additional ones.

definitions.public_repo: Repository exists and is publicly readable without authentication (HTTP 200 on 2026-10-20), so the claim can be checked by anyone.
definitions.private_available_on_request: Repository exists but is private: anonymous visitors get HTTP 404. The candidate can provide access to recruiters on request, so the work is real and inspectable on request, but it is not independently verifiable without that access.
definitions.external_validation: Reviewed and accepted by someone outside this portfolio (for example a merged upstream pull request).
definitions.documented_experience: Described in the résumé published with this portfolio; not independently verifiable here.
definitions.self_reported: A metric stated by the candidate (for example the PromptOS cost reduction); no raw data is published.
definitions.experimental: Early prototype or active development; not a claimed production deployment.

support_levels.note: How directly the published evidence supports the role. No fit scores, percentages, or rankings are computed.

definitions.strongly_supported: Several published artefacts in this area, including at least one flagship project with an independently verifiable repository.
definitions.supported: At least one published artefact or one documented engagement addresses this role directly.
definitions.partially_supported: Adjacent evidence exists, but a stated part of the role is explicitly not claimed (see `caveat`).

limitations: No published research, peer-reviewed papers, certifications, awards, or employer-scale production deployments are claimed.
Model training, fine-tuning, evaluation benchmarks and MLOps are not claimed.
ML Engineer relevance is partial: no documented model training or deployed ML services.

Mobile GUI Automation Agent (Agentic-hinge) and Pocket Typist are private repositories (checked 2026-10-20), so an anonymous visitor gets a 404; both are real repositories and read access can be provided to recruiters on request, but until then those two rest on the owner's own description. AgentOS is public and verifiable.
The ~40% infrastructure improvement and the PromptOS 80–85% cost figure are self-reported; no raw data is published.
Dynamic statistics (GitHub, LeetCode) were last verified 2026-09-30 and may change.
